subject: Ciências
description_pt: Comparar diferentes processos reprodutivos em plantas e animais em relação aos mecanismos adaptativos e evolutivos.

components.description_pt: Descrever diferentes processos reprodutivos encontrados em plantas e animais
components.description_en: Describe different reproductive processes found in plants and animals
components.cc_component_description: Identify and describe multiple reproductive strategies used by plants, including sexual and asexual reproduction

components.description_pt: Comparar os resultados genéticos da reprodução sexual versus assexuada quanto à variação de descendentes
components.description_en: Compare the genetic outcomes of sexual versus asexual reproduction for offspring variation
components.cc_component_description: Compare the genetic outcomes of sexual versus asexual reproduction for offspring variation

components.description_pt: Relacionar estratégias reprodutivas específicas em plantas e animais com suas vantagens adaptativas
components.description_en: Relate specific reproductive strategies in plants and animals to their adaptive advantages
components.cc_component_description: Identify examples of evolved group behaviors and explain their adaptive advantage for reproductive success

components.description_pt: Explicar o significado evolutivo de diferentes mecanismos reprodutivos em organismos vivos
components.description_en: Explain the evolutionary significance of different reproductive mechanisms in living organisms
components.cc_component_description: Construct an explanation of evolutionary history using anatomical evidence from living and fossil organisms

cc_matches.description: Organisms reproduce, either sexually or asexually, and transfer their genetic information to their offspring.
Group behavior has evolved because membership can increase the chances of survival for individuals and their genetic relatives.
Plants reproduce in a variety of ways, sometimes depending on animal behavior and specialized features for reproduction.

Anatomical similarities and differences between various organisms living today and between them and organisms in the fossil record, enable the reconstruction of evolutionary history and the inference of lines of evolutionary descent.
